analysis.investment_thesis: Greaves Cotton fails both legs of the Magic Formula — Earnings Yield of ~3.6% (EBIT INR 137 Cr / EV ~INR 3,810 Cr) is less than half the 6% minimum, and ROCE of 5.13% is a fraction of the 20% threshold required to signal a good business. With free cash flow negative in 4 of the last 5 years and net losses in 3 of the last 5, there is no formula-grade earnings power to buy cheaply.
key_strengths: Low leverage (D/E 0.12) provides some balance sheet buffer during the EV transition burn
Strong promoter holding at 55.8% signals skin-in-the-game alignment
Revenue recovering toward INR 2,918 Cr in 2025, with EBITDA trending up from the 2022 trough of INR 44 Cr
key_risks: ROIC/ROCE at 5.1% is catastrophically below cost of capital — the business is destroying value
Free cash flow has been negative INR 553 Cr cumulatively over 2022-2025; cash burn is structural, not cyclical
EV segment (Ampere) triggered a ~INR 270 Cr impairment in 2024; operating margin collapsed from 13.5% (2019) to 3.9% (2025)
red_flags: Net losses in FY21, FY22, FY24, and near-zero profit in FY25 (-INR 6 Cr) — Magic Formula requires positive EBIT to even apply
OCF positive in only 1 of last 5 years; the business cannot self-fund without external capital
Finance costs growing at 36% CAGR (INR 1 Cr → INR 16 Cr) while borrowings jumped to INR 185 Cr — debt dependency is rising
P/E of 34.6x is essentially meaningless on near-zero earnings; at normalized margins the stock is not cheap
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Greaves Cotton produces disqualifying numbers on both axes. Earnings Yield: EBIT of INR 137 Cr against an Enterprise Value of roughly INR 3,810 Cr (market cap INR 3,760 Cr + borrowings INR 185 Cr − cash INR 135 Cr) yields just 3.6% — far below the 6% floor I require and nowhere near the 12-15% that signals a true bargain. Return on Capital: the company's own reported ROCE is 5.1%, operating margins have compressed from a decent 13.5% in FY19 to a thin 3.94% today. A business earning 5% on its capital when the cost of that capital is likely 12-14% is systematically shrinking shareholder value, not creating it.

The deeper issue is structural, not cyclical. The pivot into electric vehicles via Ampere has been a cash furnace — cumulative negative FCF of ~INR 553 Cr from FY22-FY25, an impairment charge large enough to wipe out FY24 earnings entirely (-INR 270 Cr in "other income"), and operating cash flow positive in just 1 of the last 5 years. Even if the EV turnaround materialises, the Magic Formula demands evidence of high returns on capital today, not a speculative promise of future margins. Until EBIT/EV crosses 10%+ and ROCE clears 20%, this does not belong in a formula-driven portfolio.
